Mesillat Yesharim 19:90: The first is: "whatever the Merciful One does is for the good" (Berachot 60b), for even that pain and that distress that appears to his own eyes as evil is not, in truth, anything but genuine good — like the parable of the physician who cuts away flesh or a limb that has become corrupted, so that the rest of the body may become healthy and not die; for even though the act appears cruel at first glance, it is in truth nothing but compassion, to benefit the patient in the end, and the sick person does not remove his love from the physician on account of this act, but on the contrary, will love him all the more.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:91: So it is with this matter: when a person considers that everything the Holy One, blessed be He, does with him is done for his good, whether it concerns his body or his money, and even though he does not see or understand how this is his good, it is certainly his good — his love will not weaken because of any distress or any pain, but on the contrary, it will grow ever stronger and increase within him.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:92: But those who possess true understanding do not even need this reasoning, for they do not intend anything for themselves at all; rather, all their prayer is to magnify the honor of the Name, blessed be He, and to give satisfaction before Him. And however much obstacles grow strong against them, so that they need even more strength to overcome them, their hearts will grow bold and they will rejoice to demonstrate the strength of their faith — like an army commander noted for his valor, who always chooses for himself the fiercer battle, in order to demonstrate his strength in its victory.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:93: And this matter is already familiar with every human lover, who rejoices when the opportunity arises for him to show the one he loves how far the intensity of his love reaches.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:94: Let us now explain the branches of love — the three I have mentioned: cleaving, joy, and zealousness.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:95: Cleaving is that a person's heart should attach itself so entirely to the Name, blessed be He, that it no longer turns to look at, or pay heed to, anything else at all. This is what Solomon's parable refers to in his words (Proverbs 5:19): "A loving hind and a graceful doe; let her breasts satisfy you always; be captivated always with her love." And in the Gemara they said, of blessed memory (Eruvin 54b): they said of Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat that he would sit and engage in Torah in the lower marketplace of Tzippori while his sheet lay in the upper marketplace of Tzippori. Now, the ultimate goal of this trait is for a person to cleave in this way to his Creator at every time and every hour; but at the very least, at the time of service, if he loves his Creator, he will certainly have this cleaving.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:96: And in the Yerushalmi they said: Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa was standing and praying, and a poisonous lizard came and bit him, but he did not interrupt his prayer, etc. His students said to him, Rabbi, did you not feel it? He said to them: May whatever happens to me not disturb me — since my heart was concentrated on the prayer, I did not feel it (Berachot 33a).
Mesillat Yesharim 19:97: And concerning cleaving we were warned in the Torah many times (Deuteronomy 19:9, 11:22, 10:20, 30:20): "to love the Lord your God, etc."; "and to cleave to Him"; "and to Him you shall cleave"; "and to Him you shall cleave" — and David said (Psalms 63:9): "My soul cleaves after You." And the matter of all these verses is one: the cleaving whereby a person attaches himself to Him, blessed be He, so that he is unable to separate or move away from Him.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:98: And they said, of blessed memory (Bereishit Rabbah 80): Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said, in three expressions of affection the Holy One, blessed be He, cherished Israel, and we learn from them, etc.: in cleaving, in longing, and in desiring — and these are exactly the branches of essential love, namely, the yearning I have mentioned, and the cleaving, and the contentment and delight found in occupying oneself with the affairs of the beloved.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:99: The second is joy, which is a great fundamental in service. This is what David warns and says (Psalms 100:2): "Serve the Lord with joy; come before Him with singing." And it says (ibid. 68:4): "But the righteous shall be glad; they shall exult before God, and rejoice with joy." And our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Shabbat 30b): the Divine Presence rests only in the midst of the joy of a commandment. And on the verse we mentioned above, "Serve the Lord with joy," they said in the Midrash: Rabbi said, when you stand to pray, let your heart be joyful that you are praying to a God without equal.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:100: For this is the true joy — that a person's heart should be exultant that he merits to serve before a Master, blessed be He, unequaled, and to occupy himself with His Torah and His commandments, which are true perfection and eternal preciousness. Solomon said in the parable of wisdom (Song of Songs 1:4): "Draw me, we will run after You; the king has brought me into his chambers; we will be glad and rejoice in You." For the more a person merits to enter deeper within the chambers of the knowledge of His greatness, blessed be He, the more joy will grow within him, and his heart will exult within him. And it says (Psalms 149:2): "Let Israel rejoice in his Maker; let the children of Zion be glad in their King."
Mesillat Yesharim 19:101: And David, who had already attained this rank to a great degree, said (ibid. 104:34): "May my meditation be pleasing to Him; I will rejoice in the Lord." And he said (ibid. 43:4): "Then I will go to the altar of God, to God my exceeding joy, and I will praise You upon the harp, O God, my God." And he said (ibid. 71:23): "My lips shall greatly rejoice when I sing to You, and my soul, which You have redeemed."
Mesillat Yesharim 19:102: That is, joy was growing so strong within him that his very lips would move of themselves and sing while he occupied himself with His praises, blessed be He, all out of the great fervor of his soul, which burned in its joy before Him — this is what he concludes with: "and my soul, which You have redeemed."
Mesillat Yesharim 19:103: And we find that the Holy One, blessed be He, rebuked Israel because they were lacking in this condition in their service — this is what is said (Deuteronomy 28:47): "because you did not serve the Lord your God with joy and gladness of heart."
Mesillat Yesharim 19:104: And David, because he saw Israel at the time of their voluntary offering for the building of the Temple already reaching this level, prayed for them that this good trait would be sustained in them and never depart — this is what is written (I Chronicles 29:17-18): "And now, I have seen with joy Your people who are present here offering willingly to You. O Lord, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, our fathers, keep this forever in the imagination of the thoughts of the heart of Your people, and direct their heart to You."
Mesillat Yesharim 19:105: The third branch is zealousness — that a person should be zealous for the sake of His holy Name, hating those who hate Him, and striving to subdue them as much as he can, so that His service, blessed be He, may be performed and His honor increased.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:106: This is what David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 139:21-22): "Do I not hate them, O Lord, that hate You? And do I not strive with those who rise up against You? I hate them with the utmost hatred, etc." And Elijah said (I Kings 19:10): "I have been very zealous for the Lord God of Hosts, etc." And we have already seen what he merited for his zealousness for his God, as Scripture says (Numbers 25:13): "because he was zealous for his God, and made atonement for the children of Israel."
Mesillat Yesharim 19:107: And our Sages, of blessed memory, have already spoken at length (Shabbat 55a) concerning one who has the power to protest and does not protest, and they decreed his judgment to be that he is held accountable together with the sinners themselves in their sin. And in the Midrash on Lamentations they said: "her princes were like harts" (Lamentations 1:6) — just as these harts, in the heat of the sun, turn their faces one under the other, so the great men of Israel would see a matter of transgression and turn their faces away from it; the Holy One, blessed be He, said to them: The hour will come, and I will do the same to them.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:108: And this is simple, for whoever loves his fellow cannot bear to see his fellow struck or insulted, and will certainly come to his aid; so too whoever loves His Name, blessed be He, cannot bear to see it desecrated, God forbid, or His commandments transgressed.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:109: This is what Solomon said (Proverbs 28:4): "They who forsake the Torah praise the wicked, but such as keep the Torah contend with them." For those who praise the wicked man in his wickedness and do not rebuke him to his face for his fault are forsakers of the Torah, and allow it to be desecrated, God forbid; but those who keep it, striving to uphold it, will certainly contend with them, unable to restrain themselves and remain silent. And the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Job (Job 40:11-13): "Pour forth the overflowings of your anger, and look upon everyone who is proud, and abase him. Look on everyone who is proud, and bring him low, and tread down the wicked in their place. Hide them in the dust together; bind their faces in the hidden place" — for this is the strength of love that whoever truly loves his Creator is capable of displaying. And it says (Psalms 97:10): "You who love the Lord, hate evil."
Mesillat Yesharim 19:110: Now, we have explained up to here the piety that depends on the deed and the manner of its performance; let us now explain that which depends on the intention.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:111: And we have already spoken above concerning the matter of "for its own sake" and "not for its own sake" according to their levels.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:112: However, it is certainly true that whoever intends, in his service, to purify his soul before his Creator, so as to merit sitting before His face among the upright and the pious, to behold the pleasantness of the Lord and to visit His sanctuary, and to receive the reward that is in the World to Come, we cannot say that this intention is bad.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:113: But we also cannot say that it is the best, for as long as a person intends his own good, in the end his service is for his own need.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:114: But the true intention found among the pious, who labored and strove to attain it, is that a person should serve solely so that the honor of the Master, blessed be He, may grow and increase.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:115: And this will come about after he has grown strong in love toward Him, blessed be He, and will covet and desire the magnification of His honor, and will grieve at anything that diminishes it; for then he will perform his service for this purpose, that at least on his own part, His honor, blessed be He, will be increased.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:116: And he will desire that all other people be the same, and will grieve and sigh over what other people diminish it, and all the more so over what he himself diminishes it, unwittingly, or under duress, or through the weakness of nature which makes it hard for him to guard himself from sins at all times — in the vein of the verse (Ecclesiastes 7:20): "For there is not a righteous man upon earth who does good and does not sin."
Mesillat Yesharim 19:117: And this matter was explained in the Tanna DeVei Eliyahu, of blessed memory, where they said: any sage of Israel who has words of Torah in their truth, and who sighs over the honor of the Holy One, blessed be He, and over the honor of Israel, all his days, and who longs and grieves for the honor of Jerusalem and the honor of the Temple, and for the redemption soon to sprout forth, and for the ingathering of the exiles, merits the Holy Spirit in his words, etc.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:118: You thus learn that this is the superior intention, entirely removed from any self-interest, and is directed solely toward the honor of the Omnipresent and the sanctification of His Name, blessed be He, which is sanctified through His creatures when they do His will.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:119: And concerning this they said (Zohar, Ki Tetzei): who is a pious man? One who is pious with his Maker. Now, such a pious person, besides the service he performs through the deeds of the commandments with this intention, must certainly grieve constantly, with real grief, over the exile and the destruction, because of the diminishment they cause, as it were, to His honor, blessed be He, and must long for the redemption, since through it there will be an elevation to the honor of the Name, blessed be He. This is what the Tanna DeVei Eliyahu said, which we cited above: "and longs and grieves for the honor of Jerusalem, etc."; and he should always pray for the redemption of the children of Israel and for the restoration of the honor of Heaven to its elevation.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:120: And should a person say: who am I, and of what significance am I, that I should pray over the exile and over Jerusalem, etc. — will the exiles be gathered and the redemption sprout forth because of my prayer?
Mesillat Yesharim 19:121: His answer is at hand, like what we learned (Sanhedrin 37a): therefore man was created alone, so that each person could say, the world was created for my sake. And it is already a satisfaction before Him, blessed be He, that His children should be requesting and praying for this; and even if their request is not fulfilled, because the time has not yet arrived, or for whatever reason it may be, they have done their part, and the Holy One, blessed be He, rejoices in this.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:122: And concerning the absence of this the prophet lamented (Isaiah 59:16): "And He saw that there was no man, and was astonished that there was no intercessor." And he said (ibid. 63:5): "And I looked, and there was no helper; and I was astonished that there was no one to uphold." And he said (Jeremiah 30:17): "It is Zion, whom no one seeks" — which our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (Sukkah 41a): implying that she ought to be sought.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:123: Behold, then, that we are obligated in this, and we cannot exempt ourselves because of our own insignificance, for concerning something similar we learned (Avot 2:16): it is not incumbent upon you to complete the work, but neither are you free to desist from it.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:124: And the prophet further said (Isaiah 51:18): "There is none to guide her among all the sons she has borne; there is none to take her by the hand among all the sons she has raised." And he said (ibid. 40:6): "All flesh is grass, and all its kindness is like the flower of the field" — which our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (Tikkunim): that all the kindness people do for themselves, they do for their own benefit and pleasure, not intending this complete intention, and not seeking the elevation of honor and the redemption of Israel,
Mesillat Yesharim 19:125: for the supernal honor can only increase through the redemption of Israel and the increase of their honor, since the one truly depends on the other, as is written in the Tanna DeVei Eliyahu which I mentioned: "and sighs over the honor of the Holy One, blessed be He, and over the honor of Israel."
Mesillat Yesharim 19:126: You thus learn that there are two things in this matter: one, the intention in every commandment and act of service that it be for the elevation of the honor of the Omnipresent, in that His creatures give Him satisfaction; and the other, the grief and the prayer for the elevation of the honor of Israel and their tranquility.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:127: And indeed there is a further, second fundamental in the intention of piety, namely, the good of the generation — for it is fitting for every pious person to intend, in his deeds, the good of his entire generation, to bring merit to them and to protect them. This is the matter of the verse (Isaiah 3:10): "Say of the righteous, that it shall be well with him, for they shall eat the fruit of their deeds" — for the entire generation eats of its fruits.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:128: And so our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Bava Batra 15a): is there a tree in it? — asking whether there is one who protects his generation like a tree.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:129: And you will see that this is the will of the Omnipresent, that the pious of Israel should bring merit and atonement upon all the other ranks among them; this is what they said, of blessed memory, concerning the lulav and its species (Vayikra Rabbah): let these come and atone for those.
